### DEF-253 and DEF-254 — LANDED 2026-10-16 (`nitpick-compiler_38`; worktree `wt/38b`, branch `38-def253` on landing 117's commit; landing 118; the library seat's report of 2026-10-15 09:20)

**Where it started.** The library seat (nitpick-libs_19, 2026-10-15 09:20, beside DEF-252's finding) relayed nitpick-parse's
probe06: `trait:Src = { func:step = int32(Self->:self) never fails; }; impl:Count:Src = { … }; func:drive<F: Src> = int32(F->:f)
never fails { pass (raw f.step()); };` called `drive::<Count>(@c)` -- the static plugin path nitpick-parse's 0.2.2 is written
around (PD-131: every method takes `Self->`, driven through a bound). `npkc` exits 0 and `llc` refuses the emission: "use of
undefined value '@npk.probe06_trait_bound.Count->:Src.step'". The by-value bound (`F:f`, `Self:self`) and the concrete pointer
call (`c.step()` on a `Count->`) both run. LOUD: the wrong tool refuses a program the language admits; registered as DEF-253
the same morning (the row rode landing 113), the reading confirmed by a read-only groundwork job (Opus, $4.21, through
`management_0`'s credit offer) that named the one line and flagged a neighbour it could not verify by reading.

**The defects.** D-156 qualifies a method's symbol by the impl's module and TARGET: the definition mints `Count:Src.step` from the
impl's resolved target (`impl_method_sym`), and the checker records the same from the peeled receiver when an impl answers. A call
through a BOUND records no symbol (at check time the receiver is the parameter `F`, and there is no impl yet), so the emitter's sync
bound-call branch (`emit_method_call`, ir_expr.npk, 1.0.6b) rebuilds the name from the SUBSTITUTED receiver -- and built it from the
receiver as written, `Count->`, peeling the pointer only afterwards, for `impl_decl_for`; the async twin (`async_callee_name`) had
peeled first since 1.1.12c. Beside it, DEF-254, verified by this landing's test on its first run: inside a trait DEFAULT whose
receiver is `Self->`, `self.tick()` types the receiver as the POINTER to `Self`, the `Self`-receiver test in the same branch (and in
the async twin) read the pointer's kind and missed, and the call named the bare `tick` -- a symbol nothing defines, on every
compiler since D-185 admitted `Self->` receivers, through a bound or not; an `async` default awaiting a sibling method on `self`
had the same miss by construction (an async receiver is always a pointer). And a family impl answering through `F->` recorded no
instance (`type_decl_of` answers 0 for a pointer).

**The fix.** The sync bound-call branch peels the one pointer level BEFORE it builds the name and notes the family instance (as `.`
always peels, D-098), and both branches peel `Self->` before the `Self`-receiver test. Two readers of a receiver's type, one rule.

**The tests.** `tests/backend/programs/bound_ptr_receiver.npk`, eight shapes checked once each, exit 0 at both legs: the row's shape
with the turbofish and inferred; probe06's (a failable method, two impls through one bound, `relay`, a `pick` over the stepped
value); the by-value bound and the concrete pointer call as controls; a family impl `impl:<T>:Box<T>:Src` driven through `F->` (the
instance noted from the peeled type: `Box<int32>:Src.step` is emitted); a trait default through `F->`; a two-trait bound
(`F: Src & Val`); a field receiver of pointer-to-parameter type (`Holder<F>->` with `F->:f`); and DEF-254's own shape, the default
called on a concrete pointer. Landing 117's compiler emits `Box<int32>->:Src.step` and the bare `tick` for it, and `llc` refuses the
module. `tests/backend/programs/generic_list.npk`'s comment, which said a trait method cannot take `Self->`, is corrected (dated).

### DEF-242 — LANDED 2026-10-17 (`nitpick-compiler_39`; worktree `wt/39g`, branch `39-def242` on landing 125's commit; landing 126; registered at landing 97; first after 125 by the author's reorder of 2026-10-16 at 23:35:51 -- Q37, through `management_1`: "nice! for q37, yes i am fine with that.")

**Where it started.** Landing 97's emission comparison (DEF-231, the frac section) showed 561 of 561 tree programs and 2,435 of 2,435 library programs different in text by the site table's renumbering alone, and `nitpick-compiler_32` registered DEF-242 reading it: D-179's error-origin site table (`@npk.sitep.N`, `@npk.site.lines`, `@npk.site.paths`; read by `site_path`/`site_line` when a `failsafe` names a trap's origin) numbered the prelude's sites first and the program's after them, and every emission carried every prelude site -- the tables were written BEFORE D-262's trim, so they were roots the trim kept whole: some 290 `prelude.npk` rows and a 300-entry pair of tables in a program that calls none of those bodies -- so a prelude edit moved EVERY program's text (landing 97: 561 of 561 tree programs and 2,435 of 2,435 library programs by the renumbering alone), the library side's per-program digests moved across every such re-pin (F39), and an emission comparison had to be canonicalised (`meta/roadmap/1.6/tools/sitenorm.py`) before it said anything. The plan is `.internal/handoff_35/D242_PLAN.md`.

**What the code did.** `irw_site(w, path, line)` (ir_writer.npk) is the one registration -- a (path, line) row deduplicated in first-sight order, the id `i + 1` (0 the runtime's reserved site) -- and every consumer wrote the id inline through `irw_line` as one of two call shapes; `emit_all` wrote the tables (`emit_site_tables`) BEFORE it trimmed the items, so the tables were roots the trim kept whole, every site ever registered in every program.

**The change.** `emit_all` (emit_program.npk) trims the items FIRST (`irw_trim_items`), then `irw_renumber_sites` (ir_writer.npk, new) scans the kept text for the two call shapes `call void @npk_chain_reset(i32 N)` / `call void @npk_chain_push(i32 N)` -- the whole surface of a site reference: every writer goes through `irw_line` (35 sites: ir_expr 24, ir_stmt 6, ir_rules 2, emit_program 2, ir_func 1), and a writer nobody anticipated is caught by the belt, never misnumbered in silence -- maps the referenced ids to dense new ids from 1 in ascending OLD id order (registration order, D-078: deterministic), rewrites them in the text and keeps the old ids in `IrWriter.site_keep`; `emit_site_tables` then writes `@npk.sitep.K`, `@npk.site.lines` and `@npk.site.paths` for the kept sites alone, each row's path and line read through its old id, the two lookups' bound the kept count + 1. The ids are the emission's own constants, so nothing changes at run time: a trap's origin prints the same path and line, the chain's semantics stand (reset at an origin, push at a relay), the runtime's reserved site 0 stays, no obligation row, guard or node id moves, the explorer's step counts are untouched (the tables are data). THE BELT, in both runners: `check_site_table_dense` (harness.py) and `ir_site_table_dense` (npkg/irscan.npk), asked of every module the compiler under test emits beside the prelude-trim belt (a program's emission, the verified build's, the compiler's own; never the snapshot's, the 1.5.2d rule) -- the set of ids the two call shapes reference equals {1..n} where n+1 is the lines table's length (row 0 the runtime's reserved site); a spare row is the renumbering not running, an id past the table a writer that spells a chain call another way; a module with no table and no call passes (the floor, the shim); each runner's self-check plants three cases (a dense table, a spare row, a call past the table), the harness's texts byte for byte.

### D-339 — LANDED 2026-10-17 (built by `nitpick-compiler_39`, landed by `nitpick-compiler_40`; worktree `wt/39h`, branch `39-d339` on landing 126's commit; landing 127; 1.6.1e step 3c; the user's ratification of S-119 on 2026-10-01 as D-339; DEF-181 FIXED)

**Where it started.** DEF-181 (2026-09-30, step 3's probes): six holes of the lock-order proof and one over-restriction, each ACCEPTED or wrongly refused on every compiler since 0.5.6; S-119's floor; D-339 ratified the closing with "measured on the tree first". Planned execution-grade at `.internal/handoff_35/D339_PLAN.md`.

**Measured first.** The eight probes on landing 125's compiler (`wt/39g/.internal/probes/locks/`): `pa_hole` (1), `pa_hole_dyn` (the floor), `pd_self` (2), `pf_hold` (3), `pf_defer` (4), `p_sentinel` (6) ACCEPTED; `pn_helper` (the over-restriction) `NITPICK-LOCK-001` at 27:80; `pm_join` (5) compiling and exiting 21 (`DeadlineExceeded`) at both legs. The census over the three trees: `acquires` outside the compiler's tree in four fuzz programs only (`vf0829`, `vf0830`, `vf0831` refused as their headers expect; `as0034` in a comment), `acquires <=` in `vf0830` alone, a typed acquisition in 27 fuzz programs and in no library or application source.

**The rules.** (1) a direct call of an IMPLEMENTATION bounded `acquires <= N` is judged by the body's own summary, never by the bound (the bound is checked where the body is walked); (2) a function NAMED AS A VALUE reaches nothing -- `NITPICK-LOCK-002` at the name when its summary reaches any level, since a value is called from anywhere with anything held and a function type carries no clause (D-056's sentence for an undeclared dynamic call); (3) a binding raises the held level to the HIGHEST hold its initialiser may carry (`hold_max`, where `hold_min` had let a function that took and released 1 and returned holding 9 leave its caller believing it held 1); (4) a `defer` body is walked at ITS BLOCK'S END with the block's final held level -- D-207's order is join, defers, drops, so every later guard is still held when it runs; (5) a SPAWN (`drop` of an `async` call) is absorbed where it stands and judged at its block's end against the block's final held level, `NITPICK-LOCK-001` at the spawned call -- the parent joins the task holding that level and the child waits for a level at or below it (`pm_join`: exit 21, `DeadlineExceeded`, at both legs before this landing); (6) `2147483647` and `-2147483647`, the walk's own `none` values, are refused as levels -- `NITPICK-LOCK-003` in a clause (with a level outside `int32`, which the cast truncated before), `NITPICK-TYPE-016` in a lock type's level argument (`Mutex`, `RwLock`, `CondVar`, `Barrier`, `Channel`) -- from ONE authority (`LEVEL_RESERVED_HI`/`LO`, type_resolve.npk) the walk's sentinels read; THE FLOOR (D-339 (a)): a call that resolves to a TRAIT'S method bounded `acquires <= N` -- through a `dyn`, a bound `T: Trait`, `Trait.m(x)`, or a concrete receiver whose impl runs the default -- is legal only with NOTHING held, `NITPICK-LOCK-001` otherwise with the floor's own sentence, and the caller is FLOORLESS (propagated by the widening like a level: a call of IT while anything is held is refused the same way, naming the bounded method it reaches through); EXACT IS EXACT (D-339 (a)): every call of a method under an exact `acquires N` on the trait, or of an implementation of it, is judged at N, and an implementation whose body reaches BELOW N (or reaches through a `<=`-bounded method) is `NITPICK-LOCK-002` where it is written, as one reaching above N was -- so the contract IS the summary once the body is legal, and a refused body is reported once (D-240); and THE OVER-RESTRICTION: a binding raises the held level only when the hold is VISIBLE -- the callee declares an exact `acquires N` (its result is the lease), the callee is a bounded trait method, the initialiser is a typed acquisition, or the result's TYPE can carry a `Guard`/`RGuard` (directly or inside a struct, an enum, an `Optional`, a `Result`, an array: the layout bit `tt_hasguard`, ensured before it is read, D-227) -- so a helper that takes and releases inside and returns an `int32` may be bound twice in one block, and a function that hands a user-levelled lease on WRITES `acquires N`.

**The tests.** `tests/analysis/rejection/lock_floor.npk` (thirteen sites, five controls), `tests/types/rejection/lock_level_sentinel.npk` (two), `tests/backend/programs/lock_helper_twice.npk` (exit 3 at both legs; refused LOCK-001 by every compiler before), `lock_undeclared.npk` (case 6b re-spelled: the implementation below an exact 3 is LOCK-002, the direct call under 2 judged at the contract and silent), `chan_levels.npk` (case 8 re-spelled with a `Guard`: a clause-less wrapper's `Lease` is no visible hold -- the one prediction that failed, read as the rule's own consequence), `tests/accept/lock_levels.npk` (a helper bound twice, a `defer` written after its guards, a spawn whose guard ends in an inner block; the failsafe names `DeadlineExceeded`).

**The measurements**, all READ before the record. THE SWEEP under landing 126's checker and this one over 5,211 files: 14 sites appeared (the ten of `lock_floor.npk` the base did not report -- 66:11 hole 1 (judged by the body), 80:6 the floor, 92:13 its propagation through `via`, 112:5 and 158:34 LOCK-002 (`Shallow.open` below its exact 3; `reaches_1` named as a value), 184:36 the highest hold, 195:29 the `defer`, 217:15 the spawn, 239:36 and 240:45 the two sentinels (LOCK-003); its other three sites (a bound call holding 3, the two typed holds) both compilers report -- `lock_undeclared.npk`'s LOCK-002 at 152:5 (`Shallow.open` under `acquires 3`), `lock_level_sentinel.npk`'s two TYPE-016 (19:22, 25:25) and the fuzz corpus's `cc0427` (LOCK-001 at 23:16: its `Result<Guard<int32>>:late` bound in the block that joins `holder`, which acquires the same level 3)), 5 vanished (the base's own readings of the landing's files: `lock_floor.npk`'s two controls (120:16 `opens_under_two`, judged by the body's 1 where the contract's 3 governs now; 260:25 `twice`'s second binding, the over-restriction), `lock_undeclared.npk`'s 164:16 (case 6b's LOCK-001 at the direct call, judged at the contract now), `accept/lock_levels.npk`'s 138:25 (`twice`, the over-restriction) and the program `lock_helper_twice.npk`'s 25:25 (the over-restriction); the three re-spelled tree programs and `chan_levels.npk`'s re-spelled case 8 move nothing (both compilers accept the first, both report the second's 164:21)). THE EMISSION COMPARISON: 580 programs under both compilers, 579 byte-identical, 0 different, 0 newly refused, 1 refused by the base alone. The libraries and applications: 4,061 programs, 1,894 byte-identical, 2,166 refused by both, 0 different, 1 newly refused (`cc0427`, the fuzz corpus's expiry claim: its spelling, a `Result<Guard>` bound in the block that joins the child). The program suite by hand: 396 programs at both legs, 387 at their expected exit, the nine `// argv:` fixture programs 7 without the harness's driver, by design. The frontend's 36 and the emitter's 6 unit tests pass. The manifest: see the commit (every `src/` change re-keys it; the new walks' rows are read function by function).

**What changes for a program.** A call through a `<=`-bounded trait method while anything is held is refused, and so is a call of a function that makes one -- declare the trait method's level exactly, or take the guard after the call; an implementation below an exact `acquires N` is refused; a function value that acquires is refused at the name; a `defer` body and a spawn are judged at their block's end; a level equal to either sentinel is refused; and a helper that takes and releases a lock inside and returns a number may be bound twice in one block.

### DEF-245 and DEF-260 — LANDED 2026-10-18 (`nitpick-compiler_40`; worktree `wt/40c`, branch `40-def245` on landing 129's commit; landing 130; DEF-245 registered 2026-10-08 at landing 101, DEF-260 registered 2026-10-16 at landing 120 — the regex planner's observation; planned first at `.internal/handoff_35/DEF245_PLAN.md`)

**The change** (alias.npk, 13 edits; the plan `wt/48d/.internal/t160/DEF304_PLAN.md`). A new party kind `PARTY_ELEM_ADDR` (= 5, after `PARTY_LENT` = 4), raised by `party_kind_of` where an `@place` expression (`ExprAddressOfExpr`) addresses a `List` element: `place_is_list_element` walks the addressed place (a `BORROW_FUEL` loop, measured) and answers true at an index whose base is a `List` (`type_is_list` on the base's type, `use "../type_layout.npk".*;` added for it), descending through `MemberAccess`, `SafeNav` and `Deref`, and answers false for a fixed array or a slice (whose storage does not move). The kind is VIEW-LIKE: `conflicts` places it in the VIEW/SHARED/LENT group (conflicting with `WRITE|EXCLUSIVE`), `summary_judged` includes it, and `check_access_reported` routes it -- before the `PARTY_VIEW` arm -- to `report_elem_addr_conflict` (modeled on `report_view_conflict`, code `NITPICK-BORROW-015`, a tailored message). So it is judged by the MUTATION-SUMMARY path (`check_written` -> `CHECK_VIEWS`) exactly as the view party is: a reallocating operation on `l` is a write of `l`'s storage, and the live `PARTY_ELEM_ADDR` rooted at `l` conflicts with it. `party_word` gains its arm ("the plain address into a `List` element"). Five `PARTY_PLAIN` sites (the non-local assign, the named-root `admit_value`, the `acc_call` claim loop, the ordinary-arg loop and the final claim recheck) guard `PARTY_ELEM_ADDR` like `PLAIN`; `prescan_party` pushes it with `root_ptr:false` and `register_holder` makes it live for all kinds, so the pointer-exemption (the `root_ptr` test) never applies.

The build made it VIEW-LIKE and `summary_judged` instead -- more precise: it never fires on `@l` handed to a READ-ONLY callee (the callee's mutation summary carries no write of `l`), it does not conflict with a `$$i`/`$$m` claim where a view would not (the claims keep D-286's same-root rule), and the claim-held hazard `u304i` stays caught by the claim's OWN party (`NITPICK-BORROW-013`). **What changes for a program.** A view or a slice of a local returned through an explicit dereference is refused at the frame exit as the auto-dereference's always was; a view stored or handed on through a dereference into a parameter's pointee from a block-local carrier is refused at the call; a write — direct, by move, by call or by method — through a pointer copied through a dereference, through a slice copied from a carrier, at a two-view holder's field address, through a field-address getter's result, through a pointer cast to or laundered through `any->`, through a cast or a local copy of a pointer parameter inside a callee, or through a cast dereference, under a view or a claim of the storage it reaches, is refused where the same shape by name is; a plain address cast as it is taken is a plain party beside a claim; a write whose steps the aliasing walk cannot spell is refused rather than admitted; and a `=>!` or `=>` between two plain pointer types with unrelated pointees is refused at the cast in safe code — the same pointee, `any->` and the wild crossings stay. Nothing a program that compiled before does is emitted differently; the SIX accepted over-refusals have 0 tree sites -- five parity-matched, and the sixth (r4, build 15's and 16's) the WHOLE reading of a write through a pointee-changing cast, which cannot know a round trip is round.

**The change** (`git diff --numstat b554096 -- src/` = +246/−13, escape.npk alone; 135 code lines added and 10 removed, comments and blank lines excluded; the size bound about 160). escape.npk: the `Escape` field `redef` (:93), allocated by `escape_init` beside `holds` (:277, :300) and cleared with it (:334) -- a pointer local's REDEFINITION, keyed by its declaring statement as `holds` is, flipped once and never reset, a whole-function mark; `escape_mark_redef` (:3570) sets it, with `changed` as `escape_mark` sets it, for an assignment to a pointer local (`escape_assign`, :4781, before its first exit), an `@` of it and a `$$` of it (`escape_expr`, :5481, :5486), an untyped name marked as well; `escape_return_value` (:3954) hands `record_summary` the long form's VALUE (:3966-3974) -- its error, for `Result{err: e}` --, the verdict staying on the literal (:3975) (DEF-383); `escape_expr`'s member arm asks `verdict_borrowy` of the part READ, with `deref_targets_hold` as its operand's verdict when the operand is a pointer -- the automatic dereference, `sp.s` and `(<-sp).s` one read (:5504-5512) --, and its `?.` and index arms ask `verdict_borrowy` of the part (:5515, :5529) (DEF-378's first face); its dereference arm answers `deref_targets_hold` (:5548-5554) (DEF-378's second face); the spawn arm refuses a method-call operand with no recorded type that is not a trait's name -- `operand_names_trait` (:6955), an identifier naming a trait's declaration -- `NITPICK-BORROW-008` at the call, "this spawned method's operand before the dot has no recorded type and is not a trait's name, so its crossing cannot be judged (DEF-362's hardening): the closed direction -- report it with the construct at this position" (:5582-5593); `deref_targets_hold` (:6044) reads the target where the pointer is WRITTEN in a counted walk of at most `BORROW_FUEL` hops -- an inline `@place` or `$$place` answers its root's own mark (`escape_param_holds` for a by-value parameter, `escape_holds` for a local, yes for a root of another kind or none), an identifier naming a pointer local declared by a `VarDecl` and never redefined steps to its initialiser, and anything else answers yes -- and before the walk it answers YES in a function that LENDS (:6045-6046): the `Escape` field `lends` (:258), allocated beside `pholds` (:290, :329) and cleared with it (:344), keyed by the function's declaration as `pholds` is, flipped once and never reset; `escape_mark_lends` (:3590) sets it, with `changed` as `escape_mark` sets it, where `escape_call_like` has counted an argument or a receiver carrying a borrow of this frame (`borrowed > 0i32`, :5998, before `record_dest_refs`) -- every call, a bare builtin and a builtin method among them, because an atomic's `store` and `mcpy` store through an argument (z9, z10; D-249's dated note) -- (R1 of management's review of 99f83e7), and the two calls the language makes with no call node mark at their own arms: the `for` arm (:3866-3873) marks the iterable where `for_iter_lends` (:5779-5791) answers yes -- an `Iterator` by value, whose `next` the loop hands the iterable's address (D-166), and an untyped iterable, the closed direction; a range, a slice and an array are indexed and a pointer is handed as itself, judged by its own walk --, and the template arm (:5731-5740) walks the items as `escape_children` walked them and marks where an item carries a borrow of the frame, `to_string` taking its item by value (D-168); the comments of the `lends` field (:242-257), of `escape_mark_lends` (:3584-3589) and of the call arm's mark (:5994-5997) say every call counts, the two with no call node among them, a spawn of an `async` callee does not mark and a pipe is PARSE-014 (the delta review of ee62e5b and its D-1); `escape_spawn_recv` (:6882) keeps the receiver walk's verdict, `bool:held` (:6889), and refuses a by-value receiver that holds a borrow after its by-value judgment, `NITPICK-BORROW-004` at the receiver, "a by-value receiver that holds a borrow cannot cross a spawn (DEF-364; D-004 rule 4, narrowed by D-180): the task receives a copy of the receiver and reads through the address it holds while the owner writes, moves or frees what it points at, at a suspension point it did not choose -- hand the task the values it reads, or a sanctioned pointer" (:6945-6948) (DEF-364), and its owner message for a by-value receiver reached through a pointer names the clone first, `((<-p).clone() ?! E).m()`, and the transfer `(move(<-p)).m()` "in a function that hands no borrow to a call" (:6933; R1); `spawn_type_holds_param` (:6985), asked by `escape_spawn_byval` (:7023) where DEF-361 asked the top-level kind alone -- a `T`, a `Self` or an associated type, or an array's, an Optional's, a Result's or an atomic's element or a generic struct's or enum's type argument that holds one, past the fuel (64) YES -- so such a value is an owner at a spawn, refused unless its parameter is `move` (DEF-365) -- its comment no longer says every other kind holds no parameter: a `range<T>` is TYPE-008, an `arena<T>` an owner to `type_drops`, a Channel crosses by design (D-181) (:6979-6984; C2 of the review of 99f83e7). A dereference judged by its TARGET is sound only if every target is named: the target is read where the pointer is WRITTEN and the pointer's CHAIN is never asked, because a chain does not name every target -- the address of a call result's pointee, `sp = @(<-(raw idp(@w)));`, has no root to record (the cell d1); a frame borrow stored into a target through ANOTHER alias is refused at the store by D-004 rule 3 (NITPICK-BORROW-002), which keeps the target's mark sound; and `holds` is a WHOLE-FUNCTION mark, so a target given a borrow after the read on a path the read does not reach stays refused (d5m: SAFE at run time, an over-refusal accepted under D-286, refused on 171 alike). Two roads were missed — both CALLS that run code on the frame's operands with no ordinary call node. **DEF-393(a):** `escape_spawn_args` (escape.npk) walked each spawned argument but set no `lends`; a spawn of a sanctioned `Mutex`/`RwLock`/`CondVar`/`Barrier`/`shared_arena` pointer (or any argument carrying a frame borrow) can have the task store a frame borrow through the lock's interior, which `escape_spawn_args` attributes to no target — so `pass move(<-sp)` of the lock was silent on 2bbc59f where 171 refused it. The fix captures each sanctioned argument's walk verdict in `lends_here` and marks `lends` once at the end. **DEF-393(b):** the `StmtVarDeclStmt` arm marks `lends` for a borrowy-initialised `limit<Rules>` binding (the Rules predicate runs on the value, by value); invisible in the combined build because DEF-394 refuses a template-in-Rules at the typer, so its independence is shown by a 393b-only build (npkc `7249e6b2`, `INDEP_393b.md`). **DEF-394:** `template_item_purity` (type_expr.npk, after `type_template`, called in its loop) — a contract context (`e.contract_ctx != 0`) → `NITPICK-TYPE-060`, a `pure` body (`e.fn_pure`) → resolve `to_string` via `find_method` and `NITPICK-TYPE-061` unless `fn_declares_pure`, failing closed. **DEF-396:** `for_iter_next_purity` (type_stmt.npk `check_for`) — an `Iterator` implementor in a `pure` body → resolve `next` via `find_method` and `TYPE-061` unless pure, failing closed (a `for` cannot parse in a contract, `NITPICK-PARSE-002`; a range/slice/array iterates through builtin and is not routed). #### The double-emission read of the emitter (`mech/double_emit.py`, DEF-414's registration)

`mech/double_emit.py` reads ir_expr.npk and ir_stmt.npk for every function that hands ONE AST node -- an id, an operand, a target -- to two or more emitting calls (`emit_expr`, `addr_of`, a kind emitter): 112 entries, 35 hits (`mech/double_emit.out`). Each hit's disposition, read in the code:

- DISPATCH TABLES, one arm runs, chosen by the node's kind or the callee's name (16): `emit_k_method_call_expr` (the receiver's kind: a constructor, an arena, a sarena, an atomic, a simd, a tfp, a tern, … method), `emit_expr_kind`, `emit_expr_kind_rest`, `emit_expr_kind_rest_1`, `_2`, `_3`, `_4` (the two tables that must agree), `emit_cast_values` (the kind pair, each pair's two sites its two directions), `emit_await_kind`, `emit_call` (an indirect callee, an enum constructor, a direct call), `call_builtin`'s argument 0 and its argument 1 (each cited site inside its own `if (string_eq(name, …))` arm: `string_bytes` :8525, `own_fd` :8542, `release_fd` :8547, `io_unwatch` :8552, `io_watch` :8567, `suspend_io` :8577, `suspend_until` :8622, …), `emit_member` (a declaration's value, a variant, a member), `emit_global_const_into` (a struct, an array), `emit_builtin` (sqrt, size_of, ptr_add, wild_ptr, wild_slice, unreachable), and `emit_method_call`'s `id` (a direct, a field or a qualified call; `emit_measure_call_check` :10278 receives the emitted argument VALUES and emits nothing of the node).
- EITHER-OR ROADS, two emissions of which exactly one runs, chosen by a type or shape test (17): `emit_k_drop_expr` (a thread spawn, a spawn, a value), `emit_template` (a string item is emitted :1856, any other `to_string`'d :1861), `emit_child_frame` (a crossing by pointer :5674 or by value :5683, DEF-363), `emit_atomic_method` (an inline atomic's address or a pointer's value; r_atomic_inline, r_atomic_fromptr and r_atomic_ptr formed once), `emit_arena_method`, `emit_sarena_method`, `index_base_place` (an addressable base :10547 or a value base :10550), `addr_of_place`'s `expr_lhs` and `expr_rhs` (by the base's kind -- an array, a slice, a pointer, a `List`, a `buffer`, a string -- the index emitted once in each arm), `emit_index` (a range :11510 or an element :11512), `emit_range_slice`'s base (by its kind), `emit_result_lit` (the return literal :12019 or a slot-typed one :12021), `emit_move_out` (an addressable place :981 or a value :1003), `emit_assign`'s assigned value (plain :1042 or compound :1182), `emit_for_iterator`, `emit_for_indexed`, and `pick_selector_address` (by the selector's kind).

DEF-416, THE MECHANISM (type_stmt.npk +135, type_expr.npk +23/−11, type_codes.npk +1; +107, +13/−8, +1 at build 7). THE RULE (management_11, 2026-11-01 01:53 EST; management_12's widening of 05:42:19; the reference's sentence on the row): a `move` whose path contains a plain pointer or non-wild view is refused unless a `wild` step lies after every such step; a `move` through `wild` is then refused if the path's root, or the origin of ANY pointer or view on the path, is a value binding of the same function or is visibly derived from one there (by `@`, field projection, copy or cast), or if that origin cannot be decided. THE WALK, `move_path_verdict(e, id, fuel)` → 0 / 1 / 2: it steps a member, an index, a dereference and the two casts from the moved place towards its root; at each pointer, handle or view base it asks `step_wild` (the slot's qualifier through `place_wild`, or -- the qualifier not being part of the type -- a `#wild_slice`/`#ptr_add`/`#wild_ptr` result, a wild cast, an allocating call, read through a LOCAL's initialiser unless the local is re-assigned anywhere in the function: q9); a plain step answers 1; a wild step asks `ptr_from_outside(e, x, fuel)` -- a pointer PARAMETER, a module binding, `NULL`/`NIL`, an allocating builtin by sigil or by name, a user function declaring a `wild` return when EVERY argument that can carry an address is itself from outside (F1 as narrowed at build 8: `expr_wild_provenance`, then `arg_can_carry_address` -- `type_holds_address` of the argument's type, an untyped argument carries -- over each VALUE argument with the fuel split `(fuel - 1) / argc` over their count, the closed direction when it runs out; a `CallExpr` window holds its turbofish TYPES first, so the loop starts at `expr_generic_count(n)` -- build 9, item 1 of 23:37:38: build 8 read the window from index 0, judged a type's index as an expression and refused 127 of 400 legal generic allocators by the luck of their numbering (`tf_gen.py`); `rh3a`, `rh3d`, `rh3e` and 0 of 400 legal on build 9, `rc3f4`, `rc3f5` refused by their real argument), a bare `ptr_add`/`wild_slice`/`wild_ptr`/`mcpy`/`memset`/`mmov`/`ralloc` by its FIRST VALUE argument (`builtin_answers_by_arg`, the bare-call arm and the sigil arm alike, each starting past the generics, an arity short of one value argument answering false), a member or index through its base, a cast, `move`/`raw`, a local through its initialiser -- which records every key it visits (a local's symbol, a member's name minus the base) so a later store taints it (q1, q6, q7); a `no` or an undecidable origin answers 2, and a builtin's or a call's result whose origin was judged ENDS the walk at 0 (F2, `move_path_place_kind`). THE STORES, (b): `note_ptr_store(e, tgt, val)` at every assignment (`check_assign`), initialiser, `@w` and `$$m w` of a pointer slot (q4) records the target's key as TAINTED when the value is this frame's own (`ptr_from_outside` false) or undecidable, into the typer's `ptr_tainted`/`ptr_keys`/`ptr_vals` lists, truncated per function; the move arm pushes its site (key 0) and `check_function`'s end runs the fixpoint and the judgment, so a store AFTER the move in text order reports at the move (q1, q6, q7, al6, al7, pa10). THE PASS ROAD: `refuse_pass_of_pointee_owned` (type_expr.npk) RECORDS a `PassSite { id, ty, at }` in the typer's `pass_sites` list in place of `place_root`'s pointer test, and `check_function`'s end, after the fixpoint over the move sites, runs `judge_pass_site` on each -- the same walker -- so `pass (<-p).s`, `pass <-p`, `pass (<-(raw idp(p)))`, `return Result{value: <-pa}` (DEF-371's one road) and `pass (<-(#ptr_add over own))` are `NITPICK-TYPE-047` at the `pass`, a store into the pointer slot after the `pass` in text order included (`rc5f_pass_store_mcpy`; build 8, management_13's item 3); a verdict of 0 passes; the message names the vacant slot (D-225), the owner's next read that no rule judges (D-183, DEF-416), and the roads out: a view, an explicit `.clone()`, or a move through the name that owns it. THE EXEMPTIONS: a copy (`type_owns_for_move`: the copy-typed element or field, `m7`, `k1`), a `pure` body's own refusal (one report), a `wild`-qualified PARAMETER root (`r416b_wild_param`: the caller's `(@h) =>! wild` is the assertion, D-019, and the caller need not write it -- DEF-423's row), the declared-unchecked cast at the one expression (`m14`, `m14b`, `i4`, `i5`: the cast asserts the pointee is the author's, D-095), `NULL` as an initialiser (`m13b`: a sentinel is no storage; the later store is judged). WHAT F1 TRUSTED AT BUILD 7, AND WHAT BUILD 8 CLOSED: a declared `wild` return was an origin whatever its arguments -- `func:lie = wild string->(string->:q) { pass (q =>! wild string->); }` and `move(<-(raw lie(@o)))` accepted (u1–u3, 65 on 177a and on build 7), the record calling the callee's own `=>!` the one trust F1 added; review A's finding 6 showed `func:lie2 = wild H->(wild H->:q) { pass q; }` with `move((<-(raw lie2(@h))).s)`, no `=>!` anywhere, 60 on both (`rc3a`, `rc3b`, `rc3d`). Build 8's argument rule refuses them all (u1–u3, `rc3a`–`rc3e`, `rc3g`, `rb4c`, `rc7e` TYPE-104), keeps `rc3h`/`rc3i`/`u4` legal (an outside pointer, or no pointer, among the arguments), and the trust left to a callee's own `=>!` is over arguments from outside only, `i4`'s assertion on a plain parameter. WHAT IT DOES NOT REACH is DEF-423's row: a `wild` parameter taking a plain `@local` with no cast at the call, and a builtin over a plain pointer parameter inside the callee (`ra5a`, `ra5b`, `rc1b`, legal, named beside `i4`); and, wider at build 9 (item 6; review A's finding 1), an address copied into an INTEGER or an outside block by `mcpy` -- `arg_can_carry_address` reads an `int64` as holding no pointer (`type_holds_address`, `TY_INT` false), `note_ptr_store` ignores a key that is not a pointer, and the integer road registered on 177a (`re1`, `re2`) is cast-only, so `at(a)` over an `int64:a` filled by `mcpy(@a, @p, 8i64)` is an origin and `func:at = wild H->(int64:a) never fails { pass #wild_ptr<H>(a); }` hands the frame's address back (`rh1a`–`rh1d` 60 on 177a and build 9; `rh1c` with no `#` and no `=>!` anywhere) -- and two owners of one body by `mcpy(@a, @b, 16i64)`, `mmov` or a `memset` over plain `@local` strings (`rh4a`–`rh4e` 74, the trap once the drops run; `rh5a`–`rh5d`: the laundered header reads 66 or 60 with no drop); the row's options must cover both. HOW F2 FAILS: it ends a path only after `ptr_from_outside` said yes, so an own-rooted `#ptr_add<T>(v.items, i)` (`v` a value binding, `pa7`) is still 2 and `#wild_slice<T>(@arr =>! wild T->, n)` is still 2. HOW THE ARGUMENT RULE FAILS: by its fuel -- a chain of about six `wild`-returning calls with two or more pointer arguments exhausts it (64 → 31 → 15 → 7 → 3 → 1 → 0) and the walk fails closed, TYPE-104 on a legal program (`rc3j`, `rc3k`, `rc3l`; ruled (a) at 21:12:38, the post-180 list; before the split the walk was exponential, `rc3j` 11.18 s at 20 levels, `out_b8/rev/rc3j_pre.time`, about 3 hours at 30 by management's arithmetic); and the string exemption management's sentence allowed ("outside or holds no pointer": a string holds one) was deleted on a count of 0 sites saved (the tree's `wild`-returning functions over a by-value string, `tests/backend/programs/std_fds_closed.npk:21` and `lib/nfs.npk:61`, both `wild int8->`, on no move path; `rc3s3` refused), closed wins. `TYPE_MOVE_THROUGH_POINTER` (type_codes.npk) = `NITPICK-TYPE-104`; a test asserts it (`check_codes_tested`).

THE CONTEXT: `null_ctx` (`ExprTyper`), set by a slot before it types its value and passed through only the transparent kinds (`null_ctx_passes`): 1 a store, a `pass` or `return` in a `wild`-returning function, a call's `wild` parameter; 4 a sigil builtin's pointer operand and `atomic_from_ptr`'s, which leaves `NULL` to its own rule; 3 a cast's operand and a comparison's against a wild pointer, which admits `NULL` and judges nothing (`null_ctx_of_quals(...) * 3` at the cast, `null_ctx_against` at the comparison); 2 a comparison against a plain one, on both operands now (the binary arm sets the left under `==`, `!=`). `door_role` and `door_count` beside it carry W3's slot, set in `type_builtin_regular`'s argument loop, reset with the context. `give_ctx` carries a pick expression's context to its `give`s alone (`type_pick_expr` over `type_pick_expr_arms`, `type_give_operand`), so its selector, guards and other statements are no value of the slot. THE JUDGE: `type_of_expr` computes `judged` (the node stops the context), types the node, and calls `wild_door(e, id, t, nsaved, rsaved)` after `exprtypes_set`. Contexts 2 and 3 return at once; 1 and 4 ask `door_gated` on the value's type alone (a pointer, a slice, or an array, `Optional` or `Result` of one, fuel 8, the walk's end answering by the kind it stopped on), then `door_wild`, then `door_header_admits`, and push the id to `ExprTypes.door`; context 0 is W4's half, `@` of a `wild` slot whose own type passes the gate. A `wild` receiver is judged in `type_method_call`: a gated value as a value, any other `Self->` receiver by where its address lands (`door_place_step`). A body typed once marks once; the population's 532 door and TYPE-106 reports held 0 duplicates in one file. A `break`, `continue`, `give` or `fall` carries the state where it stands, through the `defer`s the emitter runs at the jump, to the frame it lands in, and FLOW-001 asks that same walk whether a road reaches a function's or a value arm's end: a move or a rewrite on a road that leaves (DEF-429), a labelled `break` or one held in an expression that silenced FLOW-001 (DEF-436, DEF-548), a `while` condition walked once (DEF-538), an inner loop sampled for one trip (DEF-546) and a bare `continue` in a condition (DEF-547) are refused where the wrong read stands. A jump's road past the walk's depth is ASSIGN-003 at the jump, `when`'s `then` and `end` grant nothing, and a `pass` or `return` in a `defer` body is TYPE-040 where it trapped the compiler (DEF-417's open half). 177d2b's prices `pf1`, `pg1`, `pd1`, `pd2`, `pd3` go. An assignment's target runs before its value, and while the value runs the names the target read stand still: the value moving or freeing one is MOVE-001 or MOVE-002 where it does so, and assigning or `$$m`-claiming one is the new ASSIGN-005 unless it's an inline array or struct that can't drop (DEF-571); a compound reads its name (DEF-572). THE RULE STANDS FOR WHAT THE VALUE DOES BY NAME. It says nothing of a pointer a call returned with `@l` handed to a callee (DEF-575, `k3b`) or a `Self->` receiver into a `List`'s buffer (DEF-580, `mr1`), both HIGH by kind, on main, at 177d2b3; nor of a `wild` name read as an operand and freed by a later one (DEF-574, `rt1`), or a `wild` pointee freed through an alias or a no-drop holder (DEF-579, `sb3`, `nl4a`). THE PROVER STILL READS THE VALUE FIRST: DEF-573, at 177d2b3's head, and on an `--elide` build `sf1`, `sd7`, `sg1` through a field of a no-drop struct lose their guard here as on main, the plain build right. A JUMP'S ROAD IS NOT EVERY ROAD: a clause's or a guard's stays wrong, each cell reading as on main with the same `.ll`: DEF-551's 15 (`w3`, `c1`), DEF-552's 7 (`gr1`), DEF-523's `dp1`, `dp2`, DEF-555's `cc6`, `c555s`, `d1`, `di1`, DEF-556's `rq1`, `rq1r`, `rq3`, `rq4`, `fm1`. WHY THIS ONE WALK. The ruling, whole (`MANAGEMENT/briefs/177d-held-rulings-2026-11-02.md`, "THE LIST LANDS AS 177d2b2"): the list lands as its own landing right after 177d2b, replaces the small fixes for DEF-429, DEF-436 and DEF-538, closes DEF-546, DEF-547, DEF-548 and DEF-417's open half, takes away DEF-437's and DEF-535's prices, nothing rides, and it's reviewed on its 405 lines and not its net. The small fixes had failed on attack: each was a merge patched where a road met it, and DEF-546, DEF-547, DEF-548 were found against them. So the move walk now keeps a road per state (`AssignState.dead`): a jump takes its state through the `defer` bodies the emitter runs at that jump and lands it in the frame it branches to (`road_out`, `leave_to`, `leave_arm`), a loop's head is one silent trip, `loop_trip`, and each channel a jump stamped during that trip is met with the back road (`widen_roads`). `stmt_exits`, `stmt_completes`, `stmt_has_break`, `assign_loop_body` and `give_road_note` are deleted. Its premises stand in the source, in the comment that opens "WHETHER A STATEMENT LEAVES, COMPLETES OR HOLDS A `break` IS THE WALK'S OWN ANSWER" (`bindings.npk`), where the next person to change the walk reads them. ROWS 5 AND 6 CAME LATER, BY RULING, from reading the walk's own order against the emitter: `emit_assign` forms the target's address, runs the value, then stores, a compound loading the old value before its value, and the walk read the value first. The re-ask of the target after the value failed five ways in 80 minutes, each on measurement (root-only, kept names, the guard, the guard deleted, the guard restored), because asking after the value about a state the value can repair is the wrong question, and management_22 ruled the stand-still rule in its place (the rulings file, "THE TARGET'S NAMES STAND STILL"). The rule only refuses, each price has a one-line remedy, and no independent read was taken for it: the fresh attack was the independent read, with the rule its named target.

THE RULES AS BUILT are on the rows in `OPEN_DECISIONS.md`, a row or a dated note per defect, each with its cells; `OP_REFERENCE` §2 states an assignment's order and the stand-still rule with its reason and limit, `CONTROL_REFERENCE` §2.2, §4.5 and §4.6 `when`'s cap, a jump's road and TYPE-040, `MEMORY_REFERENCE` §1.3 where a `wild` name's freed state stops being tracked (DEF-579's owed text), `DECISIONS.md` dated notes at D-323, at "Only a binding-rooted read is checked" and at "Where it is deliberately imprecise". A file moves when its verdict, its codes, its sites, its `.ll` or its exit differs from the final's reference pass, and a move with a timeout on either side is a time move. A mutant killed by time moves alone has each such file re-run alone, the final and then the mutant, under a cap of 300 s, and the kill holds only if the file moves for real alone, or the mutant runs past the cap, or past the 120-s cap where the final ends inside it (`tools/mut_retime.py`, `mut/retime.tsv`). A killed mutant's run stops at its tenth moved file, the landing's tests and its row's own cells first; one that moves nothing runs all 6,211. Each kill's first three moved files (time moves aside) were re-run one at a time, the final and then the mutant: 269 of 269 moved again, and the final gave its reference every time (`tools/mut_confirm.py`, `mut/confirm.tsv`). THE OBLIGATIONS, 8,185 against 8,173 (+12), the gate's two zeros, and the manifest's first `budget` row, `targets_held`'s `overflow` row, named as measured (line 9036)).** A BY-VALUE PARAMETER'S AND A `for` BINDING'S CHAIN IS READ AS A LOCAL'S, THE `mcpy` FAMILY'S RESULT IS ITS DESTINATION, AND A POINTER HANDED BACK OR HELD IS FOLLOWED TO WHAT IT POINTS AT. Row 1 (`9a0c382`; DEF-587 whole and ten faces of DEF-604): the store's walk reads a by-value parameter's and a `for` binding's chain as a local's, so a pointer stored through one is recorded and the growth after it is refused; a refused store into a `for` binding's field records nothing; row 2 (`c9e3095`; DEF-604's `fn1`, DEF-606's last listed face and ten cells of `fn1`'s frame): a `for` binding over an array or a slice holds what its source's elements hold: its chain is written at the `for`, so a store through a pointer the binding was never assigned is recorded and the growth after it is refused; row 3 (`a633585`; DEF-646's form 2): the `mcpy` family's result is its destination argument's value: a frame address handed to `mcpy`, `mmov` or `memset` and taken back from the result is the frame address still, and is refused where its cast twin is; row 4 (`a9d0aa7`; DEF-591's getter road and DEF-654): a pointer a function hands back into its parameter's pointee, handed on to a writer, is a write of each field of the holder that holds its pointee type, a slice among the holders, and a header's `.ptr` handed to a callee that writes through it is a write of the storage it points into; row 5 (`50bac7e`; DEF-661 and row 4's fourteen releases ("the gate attack's nine and five more", its message) and `w_xc`, a release on main): a holder that is itself a target of a pointer is still read for the pointers it holds, so a pointer read out of it reaches the storage it points at, whether the holder holds the pointee type in a slice, an array, a `List` or a field, is the pointee type itself, or had its address retyped, drawn to "the 31 forms above" of its l.97 (line 8936): where that storage is in the holder the walk came from or in the holder itself, it doesn't (DEF-663 and DEF-665, open; line 9012). Its rows were ruled on that report (management_37, Wed 11-11 21:59, line 7657): "(B) is row 1, after two changes. The rows after it are ordered by size on job B's report." What it became: DEF-587 whole and ten faces of DEF-604 (row 1, (B) and (b)); `fn1`'s seed (row 2); DEF-646's form 2 (row 3); DEF-591's getter road with DEF-654 (row 4, widened to W4 at line 8461). K1 didn't fit: "the cap of 150 cuts the list, and the rest opens the next landing in the same order. So K1 opens the next landing as its first row, measured on 177d2b5's final commit." (management_40, Thu 11-12 08:49:50, line 8595). The gate attack on row 4's final found that "row 4's slice arm made nine releases through `targets_held`, where a target ends the hop." (management_41, Thu 11-12 13:12:11, line 8805), and "Row 5 of 177d2b5 is G5a's one line": row 5, which closes DEF-661 and the nine. Row 5's attack found no release and two holes beside its claim, DEF-663 and DEF-665, placed at 177d2b6's planning (line 8907, line 8948, line 8991). Every row's cells, prices, cost and mutants are in its own message.
